```{r}
#| label: answers
#| include: false
# Computes every number quoted in the answer boxes, so they always match the
# data. Students never see this chunk.
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(gt)

crops <- read_csv("data/8-1-county-crops.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

drought_table <- function(min_weeks) {
  crops |>
    mutate(drought = weeks_extreme >= min_weeks) |>
    group_by(state_name) |>
    summarise(
      none = mean(corn_yield[!drought]),
      with = mean(corn_yield[drought]),
      diff = with - none,
      n = n(),
      n_with = sum(drought),
      share = mean(drought)
    ) |>
    arrange(diff)
}
t1 <- drought_table(1)
t4 <- drought_table(4)
co <- function(t, col) t[[col]][t$state_name == "Colorado"]
pct <- function(x) round(100 * x)
```

This is an in-class exercise. Before class, work through the lecture **08-3: Tables in Your Paper** (and 08-1 for the table standard). It is short. In class, you work through the worksheet with an AI assistant writing the code.

# Setup {#sec-setup}

1. Use the `ch8-practice` project from Ex-8-1. If you do not have it, follow the setup of [Ex-8-1](8-1-make-table.qmd).
2. Download the worksheet, [ex-8-3.qmd](worksheets/ex-8-3.qmd), into `ch8-practice/analysis`, and make sure [8-1-county-crops.csv](data/8-1-county-crops.csv) is in `ch8-practice/data`.
3. Ask your AI assistant to install `gt` and `officer` if you have not already. You also need Word, or another program that opens `.docx` files (LibreOffice, Google Docs).
4. Open the worksheet and start at Task 1.

::: {.callout-important title="It worked if"}
Typing `here::here()` in the Console prints the path to `ch8-practice` and nothing longer.

If `here::here()` prints a path ending in `analysis`, the `.Rproj` file was not recognised. `here` only accepts a `.Rproj` file whose first line starts with `Version:`, which every project created in RStudio (File, New Project) has. An empty `.Rproj` file made any other way does not count.
:::

# Answers {#sec-answers}

Open each one only after you have tried the task.

## Task 1: Predict

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="What you should find"}
A. `r co(t1, "n_with")` / `r co(t1, "n")` = `r round(100 * co(t1, "share"), 1)`%, so `r pct(co(t1, "share"))`% when rounded to a whole percent.

B. Either works, as long as the format matches:

+ As a share between 0 and 1 (`r round(co(t1, "share"), 3)`): `fmt_percent()` multiplies by 100, which is right.
+ As a percentage between 0 and 100 (`r round(100 * co(t1, "share"), 1)`): the format must **not** multiply again. Use `fmt_number()` with "%" in the header, or `fmt_percent(scale_values = FALSE)`.
:::

## Task 2: The table, in gt

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="What you should find"}
A table that meets the standard, with the rows ordered by the difference:

```{r}
#| label: task-2-table
#| echo: false
threshold <- 1
t1 |>
  select(state_name, none, with, diff, share) |>
  gt() |>
  cols_label(
    state_name = "State",
    none = "Without extreme drought",
    with = "With extreme drought",
    diff = "Difference",
    share = "County-years with extreme drought"
  ) |>
  tab_spanner(label = "Average corn yield (bushels per acre)", columns = c(none, with, diff)) |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(none, with, diff), decimals = 0) |>
  fmt_percent(columns = share, decimals = 0) |>
  tab_header(title = "Corn yields with and without extreme drought, by state, 2000 to 2018") |>
  tab_source_note(paste0(
    "Extreme drought: at least ", threshold, " week from May to September in US Drought Monitor category D3 or D4."
  )) |>
  tab_source_note(paste0(
    "County-years: Colorado ", t1$n[t1$state_name == "Colorado"],
    ", Kansas ", t1$n[t1$state_name == "Kansas"],
    ", Nebraska ", format(t1$n[t1$state_name == "Nebraska"], big.mark = ","), "."
  )) |>
  tab_source_note("Source: USDA NASS county yields; US Drought Monitor.")
```

**The trap.** If the share was computed as a percentage (`r round(100 * co(t1, "share"), 1)` for Colorado) and then formatted with `fmt_percent()`, the table shows Colorado as `r format(round(100 * 100 * co(t1, "share")), big.mark = ",")`%. Your check ("expected `r pct(co(t1, "share"))`%") fails, and that is how you would know. If your AI computed a share between 0 and 1 and used `fmt_percent()`, or a percentage and used `fmt_number()`, the check passes.

The line to explain is the one starting `fmt_percent(` or `fmt_number(` with the share column in it: it changes how the number is shown, and `fmt_percent()` also multiplies it by 100 unless told `scale_values = FALSE`.
:::

## Task 3: Save it for a paper

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="What you should find"}
The read-back check should print a Colorado share of `r pct(co(t1, "share"))`%. In the Word file the numbers, headers, the header over several columns, and the notes should all be there; `gtsave()` puts the title above the table as a Word caption ("Table 1: ...").

What can differ: the width. A table that fits a wide HTML page can be wider than a Word page with margins, and fonts and line spacing follow Word's defaults. These are things to fix in the code (shorter headers, a narrower table), not by editing the Word file, because the next render replaces the file.
:::

## Task 4: Change a decision upstream

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="What you should find"}
With 4 or more weeks, every number except the number of county-years per state changes. For Colorado:

| | 1 week or more | 4 weeks or more |
|---|---|---|
| Share with extreme drought | `r pct(co(t1, "share"))`% | `r pct(co(t4, "share"))`% |
| Average yield without | `r round(co(t1, "none"))` | `r round(co(t4, "none"))` |
| Average yield with | `r round(co(t1, "with"))` | `r round(co(t4, "with"))` |

The Colorado share should now show as `r pct(co(t4, "share"))`% (`r co(t4, "n_with")` of `r co(t4, "n")`), which is the new expected value for your check.

The Word file changed on the render, with no typing.

Check the notes too. A note that says "at least 1 week" as typed text is now wrong. Ask the AI to build the note from the same threshold the code uses (the Task 2 request asked for this), so the note changes with the numbers. A hand-typed table would need all 12 numbers retyped, and each retyping is a chance for an error that no check in your code would ever see.

Change the definition back to 1 week if your table should match Ex-8-1.
:::
